newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stays near high with sellers shy on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stays near high with sellers shy on Iraq.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures stayed near the highs on Friday afternoon with brokers reporting reluctance by players to take profits and risk going short ahead of the weekend in case of a U.S. military strike against Iraq.
At 1533 GMT, Oct Brent was up 24 cents at $24.11 a barrel, having achieved a high of $24.27 earlier in the day.
Brokers said the U.S. military convergence in the Gulf and the likelihood of an strike against Iraq made a sell-off before the close on Friday very unlikely.
The contract was even likely to reach out for the post Gulf War high of $24.39 a barrel achieved on Thursday.
Oct IPE gas oil was also up $1.50 a tonne at $221 a tonne.
"People don't want to go short at the weekend. Everybody recognises that there might be fireworks," said Charles Grey of Prudential Bache. "It's more a lack of sellers than a huge number of buyers."
U.S. warplanes and a second aircraft carrier converged on the Gulf on Friday in readiness to punish Iraqi President Saddam Hussein for shooting at Western patrols of no-fly zones in Iraq.
Eight U.S. Stealth bombers arrived in Kuwait late on Friday.
Pilots were believed to have arrived in Kuwait ahead of possibly flying Stealth fighters against Iraqi targets from the Gulf state invaded by Iraq in 1990.
In a politically driven market, there was little technical movement, brokers said.
NYMEX crude was up 15 cents at $25.12 a barrel by 1530 GMT and brokers in London said October WTI could test its contract high of $25.30 on Friday.
